MUQATIL:18:23-24/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:23-24/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:23-24/r2.claim: When you remember the exception, say God willing, before revelation comes about the Cave Companions.

MUQATIL:18:23-24/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:23-24/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:23-24/r3.claim: The Prophet is told to hope that his Lord will guide him to a more prompt answer than the promised appointment.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.claim: A future intention must be qualified by God's will; when the Prophet promised to answer the Jews the next day without qualifying it, the verse was revealed, and remembering later requires saying 'if God wills'.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says a person who remembers to qualify an oath but does not do so has no valid exception; someone who forgot has one while still in that gathering, even after speaking.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that adding 'if God wills' after an oath means there is no expiation due.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says someone who swears and then says 'if God wills' may either carry out the oath or leave it.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says an inward exception does not count until spoken aloud; Yaḥyā endorses this gloss.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says one who swears but later sees a better course should take it and expiate the oath, whether by release or manumission.

FARRA:v2p138/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r2.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means to say إن شاء الله; the omitted sense is not to promise tomorrow except with God's will.

FARRA:v2p138/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p138/r3.claim: If someone swears and forgets to make an exception, Ibn Abbas says to make it when remembered, provided the oath has not yet been broken.

AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means unless you say إن شاء الله; in a long statement, an indication of this kind suffices because one part points to the whole.

TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r1.claim: God instructed the Prophet not to assert that a future event will certainly happen without connecting it to God’s will, because nothing occurs apart from His will.

TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r2.claim: The instruction followed the Prophet’s promise to answer three questions the next day without saying إن شاء الله; revelation was delayed fifteen days, distressing him, before the answers came.

TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r3.claim: The intended exception is to say إن شاء الله; the phrase about what God wills is elliptical for saying that, with the omitted verb understood from context.

TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p223#2/r4.claim: An alternative grammarian takes the exception to qualify the utterance itself, but al-Ṭabarī calls this distant from the apparent sense and contrary to transmitted exegesis.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r1.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās via Mujāhid says someone who forgot an oath’s exception may still add it, even as late as a year.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says that when one remembers the omitted exception, one should then say it.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r3.claim: A report attributed to al-Ḥasan says that when one remembers not saying God willing, one should say it then.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r4.claim: ʿIkrima offers another interpretation: remember your Lord when you disobey.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers remember your Lord when you have left off remembering Him, since nisyān in Arabic can mean leaving something.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r6.claim: One may add the exception even after breaking the oath to remove the sin of omission, but the expiation remains due unless the exception was joined to the original oath.

TAB-FULL:v15p226/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p226/r7.claim: Reports allowing an exception after a year, a month, or the same sitting all address relief from blame after delay; none says that delayed exception erases an expiation for breaking the oath.

TAB-FULL:v15p228/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p228/r1.claim: The Prophet should say that perhaps God will guide him to something more rightly guided than the future statement he promised, if God wills it.

TAB-FULL:v15p228/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228/r2.speaker: محمد رجل من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v15p228/r2.claim: A Kufa Qurʾān interpreter says that if someone forgets to say God willing, saying the prayer for nearer guidance serves as repentance or expiation for that omission.

ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r4.claim: The prayer asks God for signs and proofs of prophethood clearer in guidance than the Cave story.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.claim: ‘Unless God wills’ is an accusative of disconnected exception.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the final yāʾ in the listed forms in both connection and pause, which the author calls the original analogical form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamzah omit these yāʾs in both connection and pause; in connection they also omit yāʾ in non-rhyme forms such as يوم يأت.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.claim: True remembrance is annihilation in the Remembered, beyond remembrance itself; when remembrance is forgotten, the Remembered becomes one's attribute.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.claim: When one forgets self and creation, one remembers God; in that remembrance, creation and self are seen as having no independent existence.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.claim: If you have forgotten remembrance through God, remember Him.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.claim: When you forget all others, draw near to God through remembrance.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.claim: Remembrance is the rememberer's annihilation within it, and remembrance occurs through witnessing the Remembered.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.claim: When connection is severed and separation remains from witnessing, one remembers God through the reality of His remembrance.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.claim: The address to remember God is not for realized people, since the Real is not forgotten; life and existence themselves remember Him.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.claim: The command means repent to God when you sin.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.claim: The great ones forget when the presence of the Real overtakes them.

SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.claim: A station above remembrance is God's remembering the servant first, stripping away attributes through His remembrance before the servant remembers Him.

THALABI:v6p163/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو العالية والحسن
THALABI:v6p163/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, and al-Hasan interpret remembering God after forgetting as making the exception when one remembers it.

THALABI:v6p163/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r5.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p163/r5.claim: Ikrima interprets remembering God when one has forgotten as remembering Him when angry.

THALABI:v6p163/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r6.speaker: وهيب
THALABI:v6p163/r6.claim: A saying attributed to the Gospel promises that God will remember and spare the person who remembers Him in anger, and urges the wronged not to retaliate.

THALABI:v6p163/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r7.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
THALABI:v6p163/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi interpret the command as referring to prayer, supported by the instruction to pray a forgotten or missed prayer upon remembering.

THALABI:v6p164/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r1.speaker: أهل الإشارة
THALABI:v6p164/r1.claim: The people of spiritual allusion say to remember God after forgetting everything else; Dhun-Nun says true remembrance makes one forget all things, which God then preserves and replaces.

THALABI:v6p164/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes forgetting as abandoning remembrance, so the verse commands remembering God after leaving His mention.

THALABI:v6p164/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r3.claim: The prayer asks God to keep the Prophet steady on a path nearer to right guidance.

THALABI:v6p164/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r4.claim: Another reading asks God to guide and support him toward something nearer to what he promised and said would happen, if God wills.

THALABI:v6p164/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r5.claim: A further interpretation asks God either to recall what was forgotten or to guide the speaker to something better than recalling it.

THALABI:v6p164/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r6.claim: Because the questioners asked about the cave story defiantly, God promised evidence and reports of messengers clearer and closer to guidance than that story.

THALABI:v6p164/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p164/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p164/r7.claim: One interpretation says this phrase is an expiation for forgetting to say 'if God wills' when one remembers the exception.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.claim: The exception has an ellipsis: do not say it unless you say, if God wills.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a delayed exception to an oath for up to one year, after which it no longer cancels expiation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r11.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r11.claim: Hasan and Ata allow the exception only during the same sitting as the oath.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r12.claim: A further view allows it as long as the person has not begun another conversation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r13.claim: Another view allows the exception only when it follows soon, not after a long delay.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r14.speaker: مالك والشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r14.claim: The apparent position of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that the exception is valid only when attached immediately to the oath.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.claim: This is guidance to attach God's will to a decision rather than make an unconditional commitment, since an obstacle might prevent it and turn the promise into a lie; Moses was not lying when he failed to be patient because he qualified his promise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.claim: Mentioning God's will acknowledges that He governs actions through His power and assistance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.claim: For an oath, adding إن شاء الله can remove the need for expiation if the oath is broken.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r5.claim: Remember your Lord when you forget something and He may remind you; otherwise He may guide you to what is better than what you forgot, according to an unnamed theologian.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r6.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r6.claim: Remember your Lord when angry so that remembrance removes anger.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r7.claim: Remember your Lord if you forgot to qualify an oath with God's will.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r8.claim: The commanded remembrance may be the remaining words of the verse asking God to guide one toward better judgment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r9.claim: Alternatively, it may be saying إن شاء الله after forgetting it in an oath.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.claim: When forgetfulness comes, remembrance should strip one's purpose from the homeland of heedlessness; noticing one's own remembrance is itself a flaw.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.claim: Remember God after forgetting one's share in Him or forgetting everything besides Him.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.claim: The youths were so absorbed they did not notice time passing; God nevertheless counted their breaths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r1.speaker: أكثر الناس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r1.claim: Most interpreters take “remember your Lord when you forget” to mean: if you forgot to say “if God wills,” say it when you remember.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r10.claim: There is no disagreement about a connected qualification; disagreement concerns one separated from the oath.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r11.speaker: الحسن عن قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r11.claim: A qualification counts when spoken continuously with the oath and with no intervening speech.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r12.speaker: طاووس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r12.claim: A separated qualification still counts as long as the person remains in the same session.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r13.speaker: حماد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r13.claim: A qualification kept only in one's mind does not count until one hears oneself say it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r14.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r14.claim: Moving the tongue to articulate the qualification is sufficient.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r15.speaker: مذهب الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r15.claim: In the Shafi'i school, forgetting to connect a qualification makes it too late for divorce, emancipation, and other oaths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r16.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r16.claim: Some Shafi'i associates say it helps only if the person intended the qualification when starting the oath and then connected it; a later decision does not help.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r17.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r17.claim: Al-Wahidi's correct view is that a qualification benefits the swearer when it is connected to the oath.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r2.claim: The forgotten qualification may be supplied even after a month.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r3.claim: For a promise without an oath, forgetting the qualification violates the command, but saying it later when remembered removes blame.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r4.claim: If someone forgets “if God wills” after promising to act tomorrow, he should say it when he remembers, even after a day, month, or year.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r5.claim: When you remember, make the qualification.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r6.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r6.claim: The qualification remains available whenever the person remembers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r7.claim: These delayed qualifications concern promises without oaths; an oath qualified by a connected “if God wills” is not broken.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r8.claim: The Prophet said that whoever swears and says “if God wills” does not break the oath.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r9.speaker: ابن عمر عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p582/r9.claim: The Prophet said that a person who swears and says “if God wills” has the choice to act or not.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r1.claim: A report says one may qualify an oath whenever remembered, however much time has passed; al-Wahidi rejects it because a qualification must be attached to the speech it qualifies.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r2.claim: The verse concerns a promise, not an oath: the Prophet had promised to answer about the Cave Companions the next day but had not sworn.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r3.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r3.claim: The Prophet said that one who swears and then sees a better course should take it and expiate the oath.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r4.claim: If someone swears without intending an exception, the oath is established and cannot be undone by a later statement; a connected exception prevents it from becoming established.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r5.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r5.claim: Many exegetes read “remember your Lord when you forget” as a new statement about something other than the qualification, which was already said in its proper connected place.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r6.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r6.claim: “Remember your Lord when you forget” means when you become angry; remembering God removes anger caused by forgetting to remember Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r7.speaker: السدي والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r7.claim: The command concerns someone who forgets a prayer: he must pray it when he remembers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p585/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Ibn Abbas was too learned to let an unconnected qualification cancel an oath; his statement likely concerned a promise without an oath and was misreported as applying to oaths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r1.claim: The Prophet asks to be guided to signs and proofs of prophethood clearer and more guiding than the story of the Cave Companions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r2.claim: God answered by giving the Prophet knowledge of messengers' unseen histories, clearer proof and guidance than the Cave story.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r3.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r3.claim: The statement is to be said with the delayed qualification, as an expiation for forgetting it: the Prophet asks God to guide him so he will not forget again.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r4.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p586/r4.claim: Alternatively, when the Prophet forgets something, he is told to remember God and ask to be reminded or guided to something better than what he forgot.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r2.claim: If he forgets to say “if God wills,” he should remember God and say it when he recalls.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r3.claim: The Prophet asks God for signs and proofs of prophethood clearer and more conclusive than the story of the cave youths; God gave him knowledge of unseen messengers and their reports.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r10.speaker: أبو علي وجماعة
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r10.claim: Another analysis treats the command as an independent sentence, not connected to the preceding exception instruction.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r11.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r11.claim: He explains remembering God after forgetting as repentance after sin.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r12.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r12.claim: They explain it as making up a forgotten prayer when it is remembered.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r13.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r13.claim: He says to turn to God for help remembering something one needs, making the verse an instruction to rely on Him in seeking it.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r14.claim: Other readings take forgetting as abandoning God's remembrance, or praise God when a forgotten matter returns to mind.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r7.claim: If one remembers that an exception was omitted, one should say ‘if God wills.’

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r8.claim: The exception may be stated while the conversation has not yet broken off.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r9.claim: If one forgot the exception, remembering God means regretting a categorical promise.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r1.claim: If one forgets something, one asks God to guide him to a sounder path; God may restore the memory or, if it does not return, show what is better.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r2.claim: The supplication may ask God to make the matter firmer in the heart and less likely to be forgotten.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r3.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r3.claim: He says the Prophet may ask for guidance to a proof or miracle better than the cave story, since the questioners asked out of obstinacy.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r4.claim: Another view asks God to guide the Prophet to something sounder than what he promised to tell them.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r5.claim: Because he was commanded to make an exception, saying this after forgetting it may serve as expiation.

JISHUMI:v6p4395/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r3.claim: The phrase إلا أن يشاء الله establishes that conditional exception is valid speech.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.claim: One should not promise to act tomorrow without adding God's will; after promising answers to Meccan questions the next day without this phrase, revelation paused for days.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.claim: If one forgets to say the exception, one should add it upon remembering.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.claim: He allows a belated exception even after a year; al-Hasan allows it in the same gathering, some only after a short interval, while another group requires it to be connected to the original speech.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.claim: He interprets remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering God when angry.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.claim: He cites a Gospel saying that if the son of Adam remembers God when angry, God will remember him when angry.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.claim: They apply the command to prayer; Anas reports the Prophet said a forgotten prayer should be performed upon remembering.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when remembering.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.claim: The Prophet asks his Lord to keep him on a more direct and better-guided path.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.claim: Another reading makes the request for guidance an appeal for something better than recalling what was forgotten.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.claim: When opponents asked about the Cave story to challenge him, the Prophet was to say God would give him clearer proofs of his mission than that story; later knowledge of the unseen did so.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.claim: Another view takes this as a formula to say with God's will after remembering a forgotten exception, and as repentance if one forgot the formula.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r10.speaker: طاوس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r10.claim: Tawus limits the exception to the same sitting.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to hold the same-sitting limit.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r12.speaker: عطاء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r12.claim: ʿAta allows enough time to milk a plentiful she-camel.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r13.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r13.claim: The majority of jurists say a delayed exception has no legal effect unless joined to the original statement.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r14.claim: When al-Mansur challenged Abu Hanifa over disagreeing with Ibn Abbas, Abu Hanifa argued that delayed exceptions to oath-bound allegiance would let people leave and then renounce it; al-Mansur approved.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r15.claim: “Remember your Lord” may mean praise and seek forgiveness after forgetting, emphasizing care with the exception.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r16.claim: Other explanations are to remember God after neglecting part of His command, or when forgetfulness strikes so He recalls the forgotten; this also covers making up a missed prayer upon remembering.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r17.claim: “This” points to the Cave Companions’ story; the Prophet asks for greater proofs of his prophethood, and God later gives him more compelling prophetic stories and unseen reports.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r18.claim: Alternatively, when something is forgotten one should remember God and hope He guides one to a better replacement; forgetting may itself be good, as in the abrogation verse.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r2.claim: The exception belongs with the prohibition, not the assertion of intent; otherwise it would suggest God’s will might interrupt the act, which is irrelevant to the warning.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r3.claim: One parse means do not say it unless God permits you to say it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r4.claim: A second parse makes the exception a circumstantial qualification: say it while invoking God’s will, as in “if God wills.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r5.claim: A third parse treats “unless God wills” as an emphatic “never,” as in the impossible return to the former religion.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r6.claim: The verse disciplines the Prophet: after Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Cave Companions and Dhul-Qarnayn, he promised an answer next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation was delayed and Quraysh called him a liar.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r7.claim: If one forgets the exception, one should invoke God when remembering it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a delayed exception even after a year, provided the oath has not been broken.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr allows the exception after a day, week, month or year.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.claim: The phrase 'except if God wills' has an implied command to say 'if God wills'; it directs mention of God's will rather than serving as an exception from the prohibition.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the prayer asks God to make a nearer sign of the Prophet's mission clear than the story of the sleepers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.claim: The author prefers the broader sense: may God guide the Prophet more rightly in future affairs; although addressed to him, the instruction extends to the community because people often need it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reports and rejects the reading that 'except if God wills' is an exception to the prohibition itself; the author says it is so unsound that it should not have been cited.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to allow a delayed exception even after a year; Mujahid says two years and Abu al-Aliya says indefinitely.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.claim: Al-Tabari interprets Ibn Abbas as meaning that a person may later join the category of those who remember to qualify their plans, not that expiation disappears; a Prophetic report requires expiation when one chooses a better course after an oath.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.claim: Al-Zahrawi says Ibn Abbas discussed a future promise, not an oath whose bond one wants to dissolve.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.claim: Some jurists attribute to Ibn Abbas the view that a delayed exception cancels expiation, and infer the same for anyone who says a delayed exception is valid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.claim: Malik and others limit an exception to an oath by God, excluding divorce and vows to travel to Mecca; al-Shafiʿi, jurists of opinion, Tawus, and Hammad allow exceptions in those other commitments too.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.claim: A verbal exception does not help with a deliberately false oath; an exception must itself be spoken aloud.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.claim: Muhammad al-Kufi says the words 'perhaps my Lord will guide me' are a required formula and expiation for anyone who forgot the exception.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.claim: Most interpreters treat the phrase as a general supplication, not a formula restricted to making up a forgotten exception.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say 'remember your Lord when you forget' means to say the exception later if you forgot it initially, joining those who condition their plans on God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.claim: Ikrima interprets 'when you forget' as 'when you become angry.'

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.claim: Although the verse concerns the general practice of saying 'if God wills,' Malik and many jurists say an oath's exception only works and cancels expiation when joined to the oath.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.claim: Ata allows an oath's exception up to the time needed to milk a large-yield camel.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.claim: Qatada allows the exception before the oath is spoken.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.speaker: ابن حنبل وابن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.claim: Ibn Hanbal and Ibn Rahawayh allow the exception while the person is still engaged in the matter.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.speaker: طاوس والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.claim: Tawus and al-Hasan allow it while the oath-taker remains in the same sitting.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr allows a delayed exception for up to four months.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi explains the rule by the risk that a person may be prevented by illness, incapacity, or a change of intention; saying ‘if God wills’ avoids a false report because the act did not occur only if God did not will it.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.claim: One reading of the exception supplies an implied verb: do not promise tomorrow unless you say ‘if God wills’; this teaches people to qualify future promises and avoid a lie or broken oath if prevented.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas associates the exception with teaching people to qualify what they report they will do, so an obstacle does not make the report false or an oath broken.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads the exception literally as ‘only by God's will’; this fits the surface wording without supplying omitted speech, and can mean that one should promise only acts God wills, namely obedience.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.claim: On al-Farraʾ's reading, the exception does not bar reports about permissible acts, since the prohibition is discouragement rather than a ban: omitting it is not sinful by consensus.

TABRISI:18:24#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24#2/r1.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABRISI:18:24#2/r1.claim: The verse also covers every act that is not evil, by Muslim consensus on the propriety of making the exception in such acts.

TABRISI:18:24#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24#2/r2.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABRISI:18:24#2/r2.claim: For permissible acts, an exception can mean facilitation, ability, release, or continuation in one's current condition; another possible sense is simply declaring dependence on God without changing the statement's truth or legal effect.

TABRISI:18:24#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24#2/r3.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABRISI:18:24#2/r3.claim: Al-Murtaḍā answers the opponents of divine justice: if God's willing only obedience made a promise to pay an unfulfilled debt false despite the exception, it would entail a broken oath and expiation contrary to consensus.

TABRISI:18:24#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:24#2/r4.claim: The hope is that God will grant signs and proofs of prophethood clearer and more guiding than the story of the Cave Companions; the author says God then gave knowledge of earlier messengers and their histories.

TABRISI:18:24#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24#2/r5.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:18:24#2/r5.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi alternatively reads the hope as asking God to remind the Prophet of what he forgot, or to give him something more beneficial if the forgotten matter is not recalled.

TABRISI:18:24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:24/r1.claim: When asked about the Cave Companions and Dhu al-Qarnayn, the Prophet promised to answer the next day without making an exception; revelation was delayed for days, troubling him, and this verse then commanded the exception.

TABRISI:18:24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r10.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABRISI:18:24/r10.claim: Al-Murtaḍā distinguishes an exception that suspends legal force in oaths, divorce, emancipation, contracts, and reports from an exception in sins, where such surrender to God is inappropriate.

TABRISI:18:24/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r11.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABRISI:18:24/r11.claim: An exception may also express reliance on divine kindness and facilitation, especially in obedience; if the act does not occur, its absence shows that God did not provide that favor, so the speaker is neither perjured nor false.

TABRISI:18:24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:24/r2.claim: If someone forgets to say ‘if God wills’ and later remembers, one view permits saying it then, even after a day, month, or year; the report is also attributed to the Imams.

TABRISI:18:24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:24/r3.claim: The author says a late exception may earn the reward of making the exception but cannot retroactively change the completed statement or invalidate an oath and its expiation; this best captures Ibn Abbas's intent.

TABRISI:18:24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:18:24/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says to remember the exception so long as one has not left the gathering.

TABRISI:18:24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:24/r5.claim: Another view says to add the exception when one remembers while the speech is still connected; the author calls this the strongest view.

TABRISI:18:24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r6.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:18:24/r6.claim: Al-Aṣamm takes the command as remembering God by regretting one's categorical assertion after forgetting to make an exception.

TABRISI:18:24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:18:24/r7.claim: If the phrase begins a new sentence, one interpretation is to remember God by seeking forgiveness when angry.

TABRISI:18:24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r8.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:18:24/r8.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi reads it as turning to God when one forgets something one needs Him to remember.

TABRISI:18:24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:24/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:18:24/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi understand the command as making up a prayer when it is remembered after being forgotten.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.claim: Quraysh asked the Prophet about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Spirit, and the Companions of the Cave; he promised an answer tomorrow without saying God willing, so Gabriel's revelation was delayed fifteen days and he was distressed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.claim: An exception is valid in an oath by God and in expiatory forms such as ẓihār and vows; these concern future acts, unlike the operative wording of divorce and manumission.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.claim: Remember your Lord when you forget means remember Him after the lapse of forgetfulness; the example means to tell someone your need after prayer ends.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.claim: If you forgot to make an exception, say God willing when you remember, even after a day, month, or year.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes إذا نسيت to mean when you become angry; Ibn al-Anbari says this is plausible because anger produces forgetfulness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation is to remember God when you forget something so that He will remind you of it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.claim: An exception keeps an oath-taker from lying if the promised act is not done; Moses' exception before his trial is an example.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.speaker: أحمد ومالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.claim: Divorce or manumission conditional on God's will still takes effect; the author says this is the transmitted position from Ahmad and Malik's view.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.claim: They hold that neither divorce nor manumission takes effect when made conditional on God's will.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.speaker: أحمد وأكثر الفقهاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.claim: The exception is valid only when joined directly to the oath; this is also reported from Ahmad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet asks God to reveal the answers to Quraysh's questions and guide him before the promised time.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.speaker: الحسن وطاووس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.claim: Another view allows an exception as long as the speaker remains in the same gathering; something similar is reported from Ahmad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.claim: A third view allows an exception even after a year.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says one may say God willing even after breaking the oath to remove the sin of omitting the exception; expiation remains unless the exception was attached to the oath.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.claim: Those who allow a year mean that the later exception removes blame for failing to say it, not the required expiation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.claim: They pronounce the yāʾ of يهديني in connected recitation but omit it at a pause.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.claim: He pronounces the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.claim: They omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.claim: One meaning asks God for signs and proof of prophethood clearer than the Cave story; God gave the Prophet knowledge of the unseen of the messengers as clearer evidence.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r1.claim: Commentators say the Prophet promised to answer three questions the next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation was delayed fifteen days, or forty in another report, before this verse came.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that the Prophet knew he could die or be impeded before tomorrow, so an unqualified promise risked a false statement and repelling people from him.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī also objects that the verse contains many rules and benefits, so it should not be restricted to one occasion; Rāzī replies that multiple benefits do not rule out a single occasion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r4.claim: Rāzī answers that saying “if God wills” is preferable, but the Prophet may have forgotten it, which would be omission of what is better rather than wrongdoing.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r5.claim: One reading supplies “unless God permits you to make that statement,” so a person should not announce a future action without divine permission to say so.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p92#2/r6.claim: Another reading supplies the words “unless you say: if God wills”; this protects a promise from being a lie if death or another obstacle prevents its fulfillment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بأن المعدوم شيء
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r1.claim: Those who say nonexistent things are things argue that a future action, now nonexistent, is called “a thing” in the verse; Rāzī replies that what will become a thing may be named so in advance, as in 16:1.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that if a person forgets to qualify a promise and remembers much later, saying “if God wills” then still suffices to prevent oath-breaking.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr permits the delayed qualification after a year, month, week, or day.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r4.speaker: طاوس
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r4.claim: Ṭāwūs allows the qualification only while the person remains in the same sitting.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ allows the qualification for roughly the time it takes to milk a plentifully yielding camel.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r6.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r6.claim: The majority of jurists say the qualification has no legal effect unless it is joined to the original statement.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues that the command to remember God when one forgets is not limited to a particular time, supporting a later qualification when one remembers.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v21p93#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa warns al-Manṣūr that allowing delayed qualifications would let people leave a pledge and later undo their oaths; al-Manṣūr approved the argument.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r1.claim: The Muʿtazila say God wills faith and obedience, but servants will unbelief and sin, so the servants' will overcomes God's.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r2.claim: Rāzī's school holds that everything God wills occurs, including faith or unbelief; divine will overcomes the servant's will.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r3.claim: The “if God wills” qualification removes a false promise only if God's will can override the servant's will; a defeated divine will cannot excuse failure.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r4.claim: The community agrees that adding “if God wills” to an oath prevents breach; Rāzī argues this proves God's will prevails and only what God wills comes to be.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r5.claim: If a debtor swears to repay tomorrow and adds “if God wills,” failure does not break the oath even though repayment is commanded; thus God may command without willing and prohibit while willing.

RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r6.speaker: الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p93/r6.claim: Some jurists say conditional divorce does not take effect if the husband says “if God wills”; Rāzī explains that proving God's will would otherwise depend circularly on proving the divorce, and vice versa.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r1.claim: Rāzī says the jurists' appeal to settled contracts is a weak restriction of the text by analogy; a whispered qualification also avoids the stated public-doubt objection while counting by agreement.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r2.claim: The stronger case for requiring a connected qualification comes from commands to fulfill contracts and covenants: joined exception and statement form one utterance, while an unqualified, complete promise creates an obligation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r3.claim: Other glosses take remembering the Lord as praising and seeking forgiveness after forgetting the qualification, asking God to remind one of what was forgotten, or performing a missed prayer upon remembering.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r4.claim: Rāzī finds those readings remote: connecting the command to the previous discussion completes the argument, while treating it as a new topic breaks the discourse.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r5.claim: One gloss of “closer guidance” is that saying “if God wills” is better than omitting it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r6.claim: Another gloss is that God may guide the Prophet to something better or more complete than the promised answer.

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r7.claim: A third gloss points to the cave story: God may grant stronger evidence for the Prophet's mission, as He later did through prophetic accounts and reports of the unseen.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r10.claim: Al-Hasan limits delayed inshaAllah to the same sitting; a report from Ibn Abbas allows two years, which al-Ghaznawi treats as a devotional benefit, since legally effective exception must be continuous.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r11.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says the command means to make up any prayer one forgot when one remembers it.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r12.claim: Other glosses say to remember God lest one forget, remember Him whenever forgotten, or ask Him to restore forgotten things; remembering God when one forgets oneself or other things is the deeper sense.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r13.claim: The address is to the Prophet but is an opening instruction rather than an oath rule; it also applies to the whole community because such forgetfulness is common.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.claim: Muhammad al-Kufi says the following prayer is a formula everyone who forgot to say inshaAllah should recite, and it expiates the omission.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r8.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r8.claim: The majority take 'remember your Lord when you forget' as a general commanded supplication, not a special formula.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r9.claim: They interpret the reminder as saying inshaAllah when one remembers after forgetting; Ibn Abbas says even remembering after a year prevents an oath from being broken.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a delayed exception as late as a year, provided the speaker has not broken an oath.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.claim: Most jurists disagree: allowing a year-late exception would destabilize acknowledgements, divorce, emancipation, and truth or falsehood judgments.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.claim: The verse and report do not prove that an exception can retroactively amend earlier speech; the command may instead refer to an implied new statement.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.claim: Remembering God after forgetting may mean praising and seeking forgiveness, recalling His punishment to motivate correction, or asking Him to restore what was forgotten.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.claim: The prayer asks for a clearer proof of prophethood than the sleepers' story; alternatively, it seeks nearer guidance or good than what was forgotten.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r1.claim: The exception means either that God permits the saying, or that one should promise only while attaching the promise to God's will; the latter is the sense Zajjāj gives.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.claim: The forms “an tarani,” “an yuʾtini,” and “an tuʿallimani” have Meccan readings in both positions, joined by Abū ʿAmr, while Medinan readers agree in connected recitation.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r2.claim: Zajjāj explains that “I will do it, if God wills” means the act occurs only by God's will.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r3.claim: This was divine instruction after the Jews prompted Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhū al-Qarnayn; revelation was delayed after the Prophet promised an answer without an exception.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.claim: Remember God's will by saying “if God wills” when you recall that you forgot the exception.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a forgotten exception may be supplied so long as the speaker remains in the same gathering.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās permits supplying the remembered exception even after a year; the author limits this to blessing, since a legally effective exception must be contiguous.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r7.claim: In a story, Abū Ḥanīfa answered al-Manṣūr's objection by saying a separated exception to an oath of allegiance could let people leave and then rebel; al-Manṣūr approved the answer.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.claim: Other explanations are to remember God with praise and repentance when the exception is forgotten, to pray a missed prayer upon remembering, or to invoke God so He restores a forgotten thing.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#3/r9.claim: When something is forgotten, ask God to guide one to another thing that is closer to right guidance and more beneficial.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet proper courtesy after forbidding disputation: speak of a future act only when God permits or while explicitly attaching it to His will.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.claim: People should ascribe action to God’s will rather than their own, since they act through Him and His willing.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.claim: Remembering God means returning to His presence when heedlessness accompanies the ego’s emergence and shifting qualities.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.claim: The hoped-for better guidance is steadfast self-witnessing, freed from veils of attributes and from fluctuation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.claim: The Prophet said he would answer the next day without saying if God wills; revelation paused fifteen days, prompting Meccan rumors that his jinn inspiration had left him, then came with the answers and more.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.claim: Reports say revelation was delayed fifteen days or forty days after the Prophet’s promise without qualification.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.claim: The exception cannot literally be part of the prohibited promise, so interpreters supply an omitted phrase that makes it a mention of God’s will rather than an exception inside the promised action.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies ‘unless you say, unless God wills’ or ‘unless you say if God wills’; the mention of God’s will is outside the prohibited promise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches the exception to the prohibition, not to the promised action: either do not say it unless God wills you to say it, or say it only while invoking His will.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.claim: The Prophet must not promise a future act without tying it to God’s will; the reported occasion is his answer to Quraysh that he would tell them tomorrow about the cave, al-Khiḍr, and the Spirit, without saying in shāʾ Allāh.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers a third construction: إلا أن يشاء الله functions like a separate corrective phrase, as if the command said never promise it except under God’s will.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says one may remember after the period has passed, like telling someone to remember something after a friend has finished praying.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.claim: لأقرب من هذا likely refers to what was forgotten: ask God to guide one to another, nearer and more beneficial course; forgetting may be for the better, as 2:106 says.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead makes ‘this’ the cave structure and reads the prayer as a request for proofs of prophethood clearer than the cave sign; God then gave the Prophet greater signs through prophetic stories and unseen knowledge.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.claim: This is divine instruction in proper etiquette after the Prophet said he would answer the next day without qualifying his promise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports a group that treats the exception as part of ولا تقولن; al-Ṭabarī cites this and rejects it as a corrupt interpretation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.claim: The verse is not about oaths, although exegetes discuss how it bears on making exceptions in an oath.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.claim: The apparent command is to remember God when one forgets; one proposed omitted object is a neglected commandment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.claim: Another interpretation says remembering God after forgetfulness can bring the forgotten matter back to mind.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.claim: Qatāda applies the verse to performing a prayer missed through forgetfulness once it is remembered.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.claim: Another interpretation urges glorification and seeking forgiveness when one forgets the phrase of exception, stressing the need to observe it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr says to remember God’s will after forgetting to say it, even if one remembers a day, month, or year later.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj had already interpreted the prayer as asking for clearer evidence of the Prophet’s mission than the cave sign.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the Prophet hoped to receive answers before the deadline and for guidance to be hastened.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.claim: Muḥammad al-Kūfī says everyone who forgot to say in shāʾ Allāh is instructed to say these words as expiation.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.claim: إلا may scope over the prohibition: do not say “I will do it tomorrow” unless God permits that utterance.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.claim: Or it may scope over فاعل: do not claim you will do it without adding إن شاء الله; a third analysis is a disconnected exception.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.claim: أن يشاء may be an exception with وقت omitted (“except when God wills”), or circumstantial with قول omitted (“while saying إن شاء الله”).

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.claim: A further estimate supplies بـ: speak while bound by God's will, i.e. while saying إن شاء الله.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects scope over فاعل because that expresses legitimate contingency, outside the prohibition's intended point.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.claim: He attaches it to the prohibition as either permission to say the statement or saying it contingent on God's will; a third view makes it mean “never,” as at 7:89.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the perpetuity interpretation after transmitting it from al-Tabari and others, without explaining the flaw.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.claim: The apparent exception cannot be part of the forbidden statement: “unless God wills” is true and cannot be forbidden.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies omitted words: unless you say “unless God wills” or “if God wills”; the command is to mention divine will.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.claim: When resolving to do something later, the Messenger is taught to make it conditional on God's will: God knows the unseen, what occurred and will occur, and even what would have happened had it not happened.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that Solomon vowed to visit seventy women that night, with narrations giving ninety or one hundred; an angel told him to say God willing, but he did not, and only one woman bore half a person.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.claim: The Prophet said that had Solomon said God willing, he would not have broken his oath and would have attained his wish, with all sons becoming horsemen for God's cause.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.claim: The passage was also revealed after the Prophet promised to answer a question about the Sleepers the next day; revelation was delayed fifteen days, as recounted earlier in the sura.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r1.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r1.claim: They interpret remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering to add the exception, then saying it when one recalls.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r2.claim: A person who swears may add an exception even up to a year later; Ibn Abbas applied the verse to this, in a report transmitted through Mujahid and al-A'mash from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas means that one who forgot to say God willing may say it when remembering, even a year later and after breaking the oath; this renews the recommended practice but does not remove the breach or its expiation. Ibn Kathir calls this correct.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r4.claim: Ikrima reads remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering when angry; Ibn Kathir calls this an interpretation by necessary implication.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.claim: Two al-Tabarani reports explain the instruction as remembering to say God willing: one comes through Jabir ibn Zayd and one through Mujahid.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r6.claim: A further report says the instruction to add the exception when remembered was specific to the Prophet; others may only qualify an oath in connection with making it. Al-Tabarani notes this route is unique through al-Walid ibn Muslim from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Husayn.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r1.claim: Another possible reading is to remember God whenever one forgets something in speech: forgetfulness begins with Satan, as in the attendant's explanation of forgetting the fish, while God's remembrance drives Satan away and brings recollection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150/r2.claim: When asked about something unknown, ask God and turn to Him for help in reaching the soundest guidance; Ibn Kathir notes that other interpretations were also given without detailing them.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.claim: The nearer guidance is to infer prophethood, divine oneness, and resurrection from broad or frequent signs rather than this rare, demanding detail.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.claim: When one forgets to make an exception, remembering God and invoking His will upon recollection is not culpable.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.speaker: الطبراني عن ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits from Ibn Abbas that this instruction was specific to the Prophet; others may attach an exception only to an oath.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.claim: Aqرب is the comparative from the intransitive قَرُبَ, unlike the transitive root used in prohibitions against approaching adultery or orphan property.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.claim: After Quraysh asked about the sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit on Jewish advice, the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying إن شاء الله; Gabriel was delayed fifteen days, then explained the omission and brought the answers.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.claim: The Dajjal's forty days include one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and a final day like an ordinary day.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.claim: Gabriel explained that his delay followed the Prophet's failure to qualify his promise with God's will.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.claim: When the answer matched what the Jews had said about the third question, Quraysh called the two revelations cooperating sorceries, meaning the Torah and Quran, and rejected both.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.claim: The Prophet warned that every prophet warned his people about the Dajjal; he would certainly emerge among this final community, and God would be each Muslim's protector.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.claim: The Dajjal will emerge between Iraq and Syria and devastate lands to either side; he will claim prophethood while denying that any prophet follows Muhammad.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.claim: The word كافر will appear between the Dajjal's eyes and every believer will read it; believers are instructed to recite the opening passages of al-Kahf against him.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.claim: The Dajjal will kill one person and revive him, but will not be able to exercise that power over another person.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.claim: The Dajjal's apparent paradise is fire and his fire is paradise; a believer tested by the fire should close his eyes and seek God's help, and it will be cool and safe like the fire for Abraham.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.claim: On Jewish advice Quraysh asked the Prophet about the Cave sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he promised to answer the next day without an exception, and Gabriel did not come until God willed.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.claim: The Prophet explained that the delay distressed him because he had no knowledge of the answers before revelation; a puppy in his house was also why Gabriel did not enter.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet made an oath, forty nights passed, then this verse came and he added the exception after forty nights.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas allowed an exception even after a year, interpreting remembering one's Lord as making the exception once remembered.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.claim: If one forgets to say إن شاء الله when promising to do something, Ibn Abbas says to say it upon remembering.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says to make the exception when one remembers.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr lets someone who forgot an exception to an oath add it within a month.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.claim: Ata describes the time for adding the exception as the time needed to milk a camel.

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.claim: Tawus says an oath's exception may be added while the speaker remains in the same sitting.

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.claim: Ibrahim likewise limits the exception to the time one remains in the same utterance.

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the delayed exception was a dispensation specific to the Prophet; others may only attach it to the oath itself.
